```diff
-     // --- Buttons: enter sleep mode on long press of BOOT button ---
-     //
-     // On this board:
-     // - GPIO0 is the BOOT / PWR button (active-low, strapping pin).
-     //
-     // Simple approach: hold BOOT button for 2 seconds to enter sleep mode.
-     // Sleep mode turns off the display and reduces power consumption.
-     // Device can be woken by pressing the BOOT button again.

- 
-     esp_println::println!("BTN: initialized GPIO0 (boot) with pull-up");
- 
-     const LONG_PRESS_HOLD: Duration = Duration::from_millis(2000); // 2 seconds
-     const POLL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(20);
-     const LOG_INTERVAL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(1000);
-     const PROGRESS_LOG_INTERVAL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(200);
-     let mut button_held_since: Option&lt;Instant&gt; = None;
-     let mut consecutive_low = 0u32;
-     let mut last_log = Instant::now();
-     let mut last_progress_log = Instant::now();
-     let mut last_boot_state = btn_boot.is_low();
- 
-     // Log initial button state
-     esp_println::println!("BTN: initial state - boot={}", 
-         if last_boot_state { "LOW" } else { "HIGH" });
- 
-     loop {
-         let boot_low = btn_boot.is_low();
- 
-         // Track state changes
-         if boot_low != last_boot_state {
-             last_boot_state = boot_low;
-         }
- 
-         // Log button state periodically
-         if Instant::now().duration_since(last_log) &gt;= LOG_INTERVAL {
-             if boot_low || button_held_since.is_some() {
-                 esp_println::println!(
-                     "BTN: boot={} held_for={:?}",
-                     if boot_low { "LOW" } else { "HIGH" },
-                     button_held_since.map(|s| Instant::now().duration_since(s))
-                 );
-             }
-             last_log = Instant::now();
-         }
- 
-         // Simple debouncing: require button to be low for a few consecutive polls
-         if boot_low {
-             consecutive_low += 1;
-             
-             // Only start the timer after we've seen button pressed for a few polls (debounce)
-             if consecutive_low &gt;= 3 {
-                 let since = button_held_since.get_or_insert_with(|| {
-                     esp_println::println!("BTN: button pressed, starting hold timer");
-                     Instant::now()
-                 });
-                 let held_duration = Instant::now().duration_since(*since);
-                 
-                 // Log progress every 200ms
-                 if Instant::now().duration_since(last_progress_log) &gt;= PROGRESS_LOG_INTERVAL {
-                     esp_println::println!("BTN: holding... {:?} / {:?}", held_duration, LONG_PRESS_HOLD);
-                     last_progress_log = Instant::now();
-                 }
-                 
-                 if held_duration &gt;= LONG_PRESS_HOLD {
-                     esp_println::println!("PWR: button held for {:?} -&gt; waiting for release", held_duration);
-                     
-                     // Wait for button to be released before entering sleep
-                     // This prevents immediate wake-up when sleep mode starts
-                     while btn_boot.is_low() {
-                         Timer::after(POLL).await;
-                     }
-                     esp_println::println!("PWR: button released, entering sleep mode");
-                     
-                     // Small delay to ensure button state is stable
-                     Timer::after(Duration::from_millis(100)).await;
-                     
-                     // Clear and flush display before entering sleep (so screen goes black)
-                     display.clear(Rgb888::BLACK).unwrap();
-                     display.flush().unwrap();
-                     
-                     // Enter light sleep mode (can be woken by button press)
-                     enter_light_sleep(&amp;mut display, &amp;btn_boot).await;
-                     
-                     // After waking from sleep, restore display and continue
-                     display.clear(Rgb888::BLACK).unwrap();
-                     let style = MonoTextStyle::new(&amp;FONT_10X20, Rgb888::WHITE);
-                     Text::new("Hello World", Point::new(20, 40), style)
-                         .draw(&amp;mut display)
-                         .unwrap();
-                     display.flush().unwrap();
-                     esp_println::println!("SLEEP: display restored, resuming normal operation");
-                     
-                     // Reset button state tracking after wake
-                     consecutive_low = 0;
-                     button_held_since = None;
-                     last_boot_state = btn_boot.is_low();
-                 }
-             }
-         } else {
-             // Reset counters if button isn't pressed
-             consecutive_low = 0;
-             button_held_since = None;
-         }
- 
-         Timer::after(POLL).await;
-     }

+ impl&lt;I2C&gt; ResetInterface for WsTca9554Reset&lt;I2C&gt;
+ where
+     I2C: embedded_hal::i2c::I2c,
+ {
+     type Error = I2C::Error;
+ 
+     fn reset(&amp;mut self) -&gt; Result&lt;(), Self::Error&gt; {
+         let delay = Delay::new();
+         self.i2c
+             .write(self.addr, &amp;[TCA9554_CONFIG, 0b0111_1000])?;
+         self.i2c.write(self.addr, &amp;[TCA9554_POLARITY, 0x00])?;
+         self.i2c
+             .write(self.addr, &amp;[TCA9554_OUTPUT, 0b1000_0110])?;
+         delay.delay_millis(20);
+         self.i2c
+             .write(self.addr, &amp;[TCA9554_OUTPUT, 0b1000_0111])?;
+         delay.delay_millis(150);
+         Ok(())
+     }
+ }

+ // --- Framebuffer Support ---
+ const LCD_H_RES: usize = 368;
+ const LCD_V_RES: usize = 448;
+ const LCD_BUFFER_SIZE: usize = LCD_H_RES * LCD_V_RES;
+ 
+ pub struct HeapBuffer&lt;C: PixelColor, const N: usize&gt;(Box&lt;[C; N]&gt;);
+ 
+ impl&lt;C: PixelColor, const N: usize&gt; HeapBuffer&lt;C, N&gt; {
+     pub fn new(data: Box&lt;[C; N]&gt;) -&gt; Self {
+         Self(data)
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ impl&lt;C: PixelColor, const N: usize&gt; core::ops::Deref for HeapBuffer&lt;C, N&gt; {
+     type Target = [C; N];
+     fn deref(&amp;self) -&gt; &amp;Self::Target {
+         &amp;self.0
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ impl&lt;C: PixelColor, const N: usize&gt; core::ops::DerefMut for HeapBuffer&lt;C, N&gt; {
+     fn deref_mut(&amp;mut self) -&gt; &amp;mut Self::Target {
+         &amp;mut self.0
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ impl&lt;C: PixelColor, const N: usize&gt; FrameBufferBackend for HeapBuffer&lt;C, N&gt; {
+     type Color = C;
+     fn set(&amp;mut self, index: usize, color: Self::Color) {
+         self.0[index] = color;
+     }
+     fn get(&amp;self, index: usize) -&gt; Self::Color {
+         self.0[index]
+     }
+     fn nr_elements(&amp;self) -&gt; usize {
+         N
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ type FbBuffer = HeapBuffer&lt;Rgb888, LCD_BUFFER_SIZE&gt;;
+ type MyFrameBuf = FrameBuf&lt;Rgb888, FbBuffer&gt;;
+ 
+ // --- Snake Game Components ---
+ 
+ #[derive(Component, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
+ struct Position {
+     x: i32,
+     y: i32,
+ }
+ 
+ #[derive(Component, Clone, Copy)]
+ enum Direction {
+     Up,
+     Down,
+     Left,
+     Right,
+ }
+ 
+ impl Direction {
+     fn turn_left(self) -&gt; Self {
+         match self {
+             Direction::Up =&gt; Direction::Left,
+             Direction::Left =&gt; Direction::Down,
+             Direction::Down =&gt; Direction::Right,
+             Direction::Right =&gt; Direction::Up,
+         }
+     }
+ 
+     fn turn_right(self) -&gt; Self {
+         match self {
+             Direction::Up =&gt; Direction::Right,
+             Direction::Right =&gt; Direction::Down,
+             Direction::Down =&gt; Direction::Left,
+             Direction::Left =&gt; Direction::Up,
+         }
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ #[derive(Component)]
+ struct SnakeHead;
+ 
+ #[derive(Component)]
+ struct SnakeSegment;
+ 
+ #[derive(Component)]
+ struct Food;
+ 
+ // --- Game Resources ---
+ 
+ #[derive(Resource)]
+ struct FrameBufferResource {
+     frame_buf: MyFrameBuf,
+ }
+ 
+ impl FrameBufferResource {
+     fn new() -&gt; Self {
+         let fb_data: Box&lt;[Rgb888; LCD_BUFFER_SIZE]&gt; = Box::new([Rgb888::BLACK; LCD_BUFFER_SIZE]);
+         let heap_buffer = HeapBuffer::new(fb_data);
+         let frame_buf = MyFrameBuf::new(heap_buffer, LCD_H_RES, LCD_V_RES);
+         Self { frame_buf }
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ #[derive(Resource)]
+ struct GameState {
+     score: u32,
+     game_over: bool,
+     move_timer: u32,
+     move_interval: u32, // frames between moves
+ }
+ 
+ impl Default for GameState {
+     fn default() -&gt; Self {
+         Self {
+             score: 0,
+             game_over: false,
+             move_timer: 0,
+             move_interval: 15, // Start with slower movement
+         }
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ #[derive(Resource)]
+ struct RngResource(Rng);
+ 
+ #[derive(Event)]
+ enum InputEvent {
+     TurnLeft,
+     TurnRight,
+ }
+ 
+ // Display resource - NonSend because it contains non-thread-safe components
+ struct DisplayResource {
+     display: Sh8601Driver&lt;Ws18AmoledDriver, WsTca9554Reset&lt;RefCellDevice&lt;'static, I2c&lt;'static&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;,
+ }
+ 
+ // Button resources - NonSend because GPIO pins are not Send
+ struct ButtonLeftResource {
+     button: Input&lt;'static&gt;,
+ }
+ 
+ struct ButtonRightResource {
+     button: Input&lt;'static&gt;,
+ }
+ 
+ // --- Game Systems ---
+ 
+ fn input_system(
+     mut left_btn: NonSendMut&lt;ButtonLeftResource&gt;,
+     mut right_btn: NonSendMut&lt;ButtonRightResource&gt;,
+     mut input_events: EventWriter&lt;InputEvent&gt;,
+ ) {
+     // Simple debouncing: check button state
+     // GPIO0 (left) - turn left
+     if left_btn.button.is_low() {
+         input_events.send(InputEvent::TurnLeft);
+     }
+     
+     // GPIO38 (right) - turn right
+     if right_btn.button.is_low() {
+         input_events.send(InputEvent::TurnRight);
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ fn process_input_system(
+     mut input_events: EventReader&lt;InputEvent&gt;,
+     mut head_query: Query&lt;&amp;mut Direction, With&lt;SnakeHead&gt;&gt;,
+ ) {
+     for event in input_events.read() {
+         if let Ok(mut dir) = head_query.get_single_mut() {
+             *dir = match event {
+                 InputEvent::TurnLeft =&gt; dir.turn_left(),
+                 InputEvent::TurnRight =&gt; dir.turn_right(),
+             };
+         }
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ fn move_snake_system(
+     mut game_state: ResMut&lt;GameState&gt;,
+     mut head_query: Query&lt;(&amp;mut Position, &amp;Direction), With&lt;SnakeHead&gt;&gt;,
+     mut segment_query: Query&lt;&amp;mut Position, (With&lt;SnakeSegment&gt;, Without&lt;SnakeHead&gt;)&gt;,
+ ) {
+     if game_state.game_over {
+         return;
+     }
+ 
+     game_state.move_timer += 1;
+     if game_state.move_timer &lt; game_state.move_interval {
+         return;
+     }
+     game_state.move_timer = 0;
+ 
+     let (mut head_pos, direction) = match head_query.get_single_mut() {
+         Ok(h) =&gt; h,
+         Err(_) =&gt; return,
+     };
+ 
+     // Calculate new head position
+     let new_head_pos = match *direction {
+         Direction::Up =&gt; Position {
+             x: head_pos.x,
+             y: head_pos.y - 1,
+         },
+         Direction::Down =&gt; Position {
+             x: head_pos.x,
+             y: head_pos.y + 1,
+         },
+         Direction::Left =&gt; Position {
+             x: head_pos.x - 1,
+             y: head_pos.y,
+         },
+         Direction::Right =&gt; Position {
+             x: head_pos.x + 1,
+             y: head_pos.y,
+         },
+     };
+ 
+     // Store old positions for segments
+     let mut positions: heapless::Vec&lt;Position, 256&gt; = heapless::Vec::new();
+     positions.push(*head_pos).ok();
+     
+     for mut seg_pos in segment_query.iter_mut() {
+         positions.push(*seg_pos).ok();
+     }
+ 
+     // Update head
+     *head_pos = new_head_pos;
+ 
+     // Update segments (each segment moves to previous segment's position)
+     let mut iter = positions.iter();
+     for mut seg_pos in segment_query.iter_mut() {
+         if let Some(&amp;prev_pos) = iter.next() {
+             *seg_pos = prev_pos;
+         }
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ fn collision_system(
+     mut game_state: ResMut&lt;GameState&gt;,
+     head_query: Query&lt;&amp;Position, With&lt;SnakeHead&gt;&gt;,
+     segment_query: Query&lt;&amp;Position, (With&lt;SnakeSegment&gt;, Without&lt;SnakeHead&gt;)&gt;,
+     food_query: Query&lt;(Entity, &amp;Position), With&lt;Food&gt;&gt;,
+     mut commands: Commands,
+ ) {
+     if game_state.game_over {
+         return;
+     }
+ 
+     let head_pos = match head_query.get_single() {
+         Ok(p) =&gt; *p,
+         Err(_) =&gt; return,
+     };
+ 
+     // Check wall collision
+     const GRID_WIDTH: i32 = 46; // 368 / 8
+     const GRID_HEIGHT: i32 = 56; // 448 / 8
+     
+     if head_pos.x &lt; 0
+         || head_pos.x &gt;= GRID_WIDTH
+         || head_pos.y &lt; 0
+         || head_pos.y &gt;= GRID_HEIGHT
+     {
+         game_state.game_over = true;
+         esp_println::println!("Game Over: Wall collision!");
+         return;
+     }
+ 
+     // Check self collision
+     for seg_pos in segment_query.iter() {
+         if *seg_pos == head_pos {
+             game_state.game_over = true;
+             esp_println::println!("Game Over: Self collision!");
+             return;
+         }
+     }
+ 
+     // Check food collision
+     for (food_entity, food_pos) in food_query.iter() {
+         if *food_pos == head_pos {
+             // Eat food
+             commands.entity(food_entity).despawn();
+             game_state.score += 10;
+             
+             // Add new segment to snake
+             let last_seg_pos = segment_query
+                 .iter()
+                 .last()
+                 .copied()
+                 .unwrap_or(head_pos);
+             
+             commands.spawn((
+                 SnakeSegment,
+                 Position {
+                     x: last_seg_pos.x,
+                     y: last_seg_pos.y,
+                 },
+             ));
+ 
+             // Speed up slightly
+             if game_state.move_interval &gt; 5 {
+                 game_state.move_interval -= 1;
+             }
+ 
+             esp_println::println!("Score: {}", game_state.score);
+         }
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ fn food_spawn_system(
+     mut commands: Commands,
+     food_query: Query&lt;Entity, With&lt;Food&gt;&gt;,
+     all_positions: Query&lt;&amp;Position&gt;,
+     mut rng: ResMut&lt;RngResource&gt;,
+     game_state: Res&lt;GameState&gt;,
+ ) {
+     if game_state.game_over {
+         return;
+     }
+ 
+     // Only spawn food if none exists
+     if food_query.iter().next().is_some() {
+         return;
+     }
+ 
+     const GRID_WIDTH: i32 = 46;
+     const GRID_HEIGHT: i32 = 56;
+ 
+     // Try to find a free position
+     let mut attempts = 0;
+     loop {
+         let mut buf = [0u8; 4];
+         rng.0.read(&amp;mut buf);
+         let x = ((buf[0] as u32 | ((buf[1] as u32) &lt;&lt; 8)) % GRID_WIDTH as u32) as i32;
+         rng.0.read(&amp;mut buf);
+         let y = ((buf[0] as u32 | ((buf[1] as u32) &lt;&lt; 8)) % GRID_HEIGHT as u32) as i32;
+ 
+         let pos = Position { x, y };
+         let occupied = all_positions.iter().any(|&amp;p| p == pos);
+ 
+         if !occupied {
+             commands.spawn((Food, pos));
+             break;
+         }
+ 
+         attempts += 1;
+         if attempts &gt; 100 {
+             // Give up if we can't find a spot
+             break;
+         }
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ fn render_system(
+     mut display_res: NonSendMut&lt;DisplayResource&gt;,
+     game_state: Res&lt;GameState&gt;,
+     mut fb_res: ResMut&lt;FrameBufferResource&gt;,
+     head_query: Query&lt;&amp;Position, With&lt;SnakeHead&gt;&gt;,
+     segment_query: Query&lt;&amp;Position, With&lt;SnakeSegment&gt;&gt;,
+     food_query: Query&lt;&amp;Position, With&lt;Food&gt;&gt;,
+ ) {
+     // Clear framebuffer
+     fb_res.frame_buf.clear(Rgb888::BLACK).unwrap();
+ 
+     const CELL_SIZE: i32 = 8;
+     const GRID_OFFSET_X: i32 = 0;
+     const GRID_OFFSET_Y: i32 = 0;
+ 
+     // Draw food
+     for food_pos in food_query.iter() {
+         let x = GRID_OFFSET_X + food_pos.x * CELL_SIZE;
+         let y = GRID_OFFSET_Y + food_pos.y * CELL_SIZE;
+         Rectangle::new(
+             Point::new(x, y),
+             Size::new(CELL_SIZE as u32, CELL_SIZE as u32),
+         )
+         .into_styled(PrimitiveStyle::with_fill(Rgb888::new(255, 0, 0)))
+         .draw(&amp;mut fb_res.frame_buf)
+         .ok();
+     }
+ 
+     // Draw snake segments
+     for seg_pos in segment_query.iter() {
+         let x = GRID_OFFSET_X + seg_pos.x * CELL_SIZE;
+         let y = GRID_OFFSET_Y + seg_pos.y * CELL_SIZE;
+         Rectangle::new(
+             Point::new(x, y),
+             Size::new(CELL_SIZE as u32, CELL_SIZE as u32),
+         )
+         .into_styled(PrimitiveStyle::with_fill(Rgb888::new(0, 255, 0)))
+         .draw(&amp;mut fb_res.frame_buf)
+         .ok();
+     }
+ 
+     // Draw head
+     if let Ok(head_pos) = head_query.get_single() {
+         let x = GRID_OFFSET_X + head_pos.x * CELL_SIZE;
+         let y = GRID_OFFSET_Y + head_pos.y * CELL_SIZE;
+         Rectangle::new(
+             Point::new(x, y),
+             Size::new(CELL_SIZE as u32, CELL_SIZE as u32),
+         )
+         .into_styled(PrimitiveStyle::with_fill(Rgb888::new(0, 200, 0)))
+         .draw(&amp;mut fb_res.frame_buf)
+         .ok();
+     }
+ 
+     // Draw score
+     let mut score_str = String::&lt;20&gt;::new();
+     if game_state.game_over {
+         write!(score_str, "GAME OVER!").ok();
+     } else {
+         write!(score_str, "Score: {}", game_state.score).ok();
+     }
+     Text::new(
+         score_str.as_str(),
+         Point::new(8, LCD_V_RES as i32 - 20),
+         MonoTextStyle::new(&amp;FONT_10X20, Rgb888::WHITE),
+     )
+     .draw(&amp;mut fb_res.frame_buf)
+     .ok();
+ 
+     // Draw instructions
+     if !game_state.game_over {
+         Text::new(
+             "Left/Right buttons",
+             Point::new(8, 8),
+             MonoTextStyle::new(&amp;FONT_10X20, Rgb888::new(128, 128, 128)),
+         )
+         .draw(&amp;mut fb_res.frame_buf)
+         .ok();
+     }
+ 
+     // Copy framebuffer to display
+     display_res.display.clear(Rgb888::BLACK).ok();
+     for (y, row) in fb_res.frame_buf.data.chunks_exact(LCD_H_RES).enumerate() {
+         for (x, &amp;pixel) in row.iter().enumerate() {
+             if pixel != Rgb888::BLACK {
+                 let point = Point::new(x as i32, y as i32);
+                 Rectangle::new(point, Size::new(1, 1))
+                     .into_styled(PrimitiveStyle::with_fill(pixel))
+                     .draw(&amp;mut display_res.display)
+                     .ok();
+             }
+         }
+     }
+ 
+     display_res.display.flush().ok();
+ }
+ 
+ #[allow(
+     clippy::large_stack_frames,
+     reason = "it's not unusual to allocate larger buffers etc. in main"
+ )]
+ #[esp_rtos::main]
+ async fn main(spawner: Spawner) -&gt; ! {
+     esp_println::logger::init_logger_from_env();
+     esp_println::println!("BOOT: starting snake game");
+ 
+     let config = esp_hal::Config::default().with_cpu_clock(CpuClock::max());
+     let peripherals = esp_hal::init(config);
+ 
+     esp_alloc::psram_allocator!(peripherals.PSRAM, esp_hal::psram);
+     esp_println::println!("BOOT: after psram_allocator");
+ 
+     let timg0 = TimerGroup::new(peripherals.TIMG0);
+     #[cfg(target_arch = "riscv32")]
+     {
+         let sw_interrupt =
+             esp_hal::interrupt::software::SoftwareInterruptControl::new(peripherals.SW_INTERRUPT);
+         esp_rtos::start(timg0.timer0, sw_interrupt.software_interrupt0);
+     }
+     #[cfg(not(target_arch = "riscv32"))]
+     {
+         esp_rtos::start(timg0.timer0);
+     }
+     esp_println::println!("BOOT: esp-rtos started");
+ 
+     let _ = spawner;
+ 
+     // --- DMA buffers for QSPI ---
+     esp_println::println!("BOOT: allocating DMA buffers");
+     let (rx_buffer, rx_descriptors, tx_buffer, tx_descriptors) = dma_buffers!(DMA_CHUNK_SIZE);
+     let dma_rx_buf = DmaRxBuf::new(rx_descriptors, rx_buffer).unwrap();
+     let dma_tx_buf = DmaTxBuf::new(tx_descriptors, tx_buffer).unwrap();
+ 
+     // --- QSPI wiring ---
+     esp_println::println!("BOOT: init QSPI");
+     let lcd_spi = Spi::new(
+         peripherals.SPI2,
+         SpiConfig::default()
+             .with_frequency(Rate::from_mhz(40))
+             .with_mode(Mode::_0),
+     )
+     .unwrap()
+     .with_sio0(peripherals.GPIO4)
+     .with_sio1(peripherals.GPIO5)
+     .with_sio2(peripherals.GPIO6)
+     .with_sio3(peripherals.GPIO7)
+     .with_cs(peripherals.GPIO12)
+     .with_sck(peripherals.GPIO11)
+     .with_dma(peripherals.DMA_CH0)
+     .with_buffers(dma_rx_buf, dma_tx_buf);
+     esp_println::println!("BOOT: QSPI ready");
+ 
+     // --- I2C ---
+     esp_println::println!("BOOT: init I2C");
+     let i2c = I2c::new(
+         peripherals.I2C0,
+         I2cConfig::default()
+             .with_frequency(Rate::from_khz(400))
+             .with_timeout(BusTimeout::BusCycles(50))
+             .with_software_timeout(SoftwareTimeout::Transaction(esp_hal::time::Duration::from_millis(50))),
+     )
+     .unwrap()
+     .with_sda(peripherals.GPIO15)
+     .with_scl(peripherals.GPIO14);
+     esp_println::println!("BOOT: I2C ready");
+ 
+     let i2c_bus = core::cell::RefCell::new(i2c);
+     esp_println::println!("BOOT: probing TCA9554");
+     let reset = WsTca9554Reset::new(RefCellDevice::new(&amp;i2c_bus));
+     esp_println::println!("BOOT: TCA9554 ready");
+     let ws_driver = Ws18AmoledDriver::new(lcd_spi);
+ 
+     const DISPLAY_SIZE: DisplaySize = DisplaySize::new(368, 448);
+     const FB_SIZE: usize = framebuffer_size(DISPLAY_SIZE, ColorMode::Rgb888);
+ 
+     let delay = Delay::new();
+     esp_println::println!("Display: init...");
+     let display_res = Sh8601Driver::new_heap::&lt;_, FB_SIZE&gt;(
+         ws_driver,
+         reset,
+         ColorMode::Rgb888,
+         DISPLAY_SIZE,
+         delay,
+     );
+     let display = match display_res {
+         Ok(d) =&gt; {
+             esp_println::println!("Display initialized successfully");
+             d
+         }
+         Err(e) =&gt; {
+             esp_println::println!("Display init failed: {:?}", e);
+             loop {
+                 Timer::after(Duration::from_secs(1)).await;
+             }
+         }
+     };
+ 
+     // --- Buttons ---
+     // GPIO0: Left button (turn left)
+     // GPIO38: Right button (turn right)
+     let btn_cfg = InputConfig::default().with_pull(Pull::Up);
+     let btn_left = Input::new(peripherals.GPIO0, btn_cfg);
+     let btn_right = Input::new(peripherals.GPIO38, btn_cfg);
+     esp_println::println!("BTN: initialized GPIO0 (left) and GPIO38 (right)");
+ 
+     // --- Initialize RNG ---
+     let rng = Rng::new();
+ 
+     // --- Initialize Bevy ECS World ---
+     let mut world = World::default();
+     
+     // Insert resources
+     world.insert_resource(GameState::default());
+     world.insert_resource(RngResource(rng));
+     world.insert_resource(FrameBufferResource::new());
+     world.insert_non_send_resource(DisplayResource { display });
+     world.insert_non_send_resource(ButtonLeftResource { button: btn_left });
+     world.insert_non_send_resource(ButtonRightResource { button: btn_right });
+ 
+     // Spawn initial snake
+     let head_entity = world.spawn((
+         SnakeHead,
+         Position { x: 23, y: 28 }, // Center of grid
+         Direction::Right,
+     )).id();
+ 
+     // Add initial segments
+     world.spawn((
+         SnakeSegment,
+         Position { x: 22, y: 28 },
+     ));
+     world.spawn((
+         SnakeSegment,
+         Position { x: 21, y: 28 },
+     ));
+ 
+     // Create schedule
+     let mut schedule = Schedule::default();
+     schedule.add_systems((
+         input_system,
+         process_input_system,
+         move_snake_system,
+         collision_system,
+         food_spawn_system,
+         render_system,
+     ));
+ 
+     esp_println::println!("Entering Bevy ECS main loop...");
+ 
+     loop {
+         schedule.run(&amp;mut world);
+         Timer::after(Duration::from_millis(16)).await; // ~60 FPS
+     }
+ }
+ 
```

## Summary

Implemented a snake game using Bevy ECS on ESP32-S3.

### Features

1. **Bevy ECS architecture**:
   - Components: `Position`, `Direction`, `SnakeHead`, `SnakeSegment`, `Food`
   - Resources: `GameState`, `InputState`, `FrameBufferResource`, `RngResource`
   - Systems: input, movement, collision detection, food spawning, rendering

2. **Button controls**:
   - GPIO0 (BOOT button): turn left
   - GPIO38: turn right

3. **Game mechanics**:
   - Snake moves automatically
   - Food spawns randomly
   - Collision detection (walls and self)
   - Score tracking
   - Speed increases as score increases
   - Game over screen

4. **Rendering**:
   - Framebuffer-based rendering
   - Snake: green segments with darker head
   - Food: red squares
   - Score display
   - Game over message

### Technical details

- Uses `bevy_ecs` 0.17.2 with `no_std` support
- Follows patterns from the Conway's Game of Life example
- Uses `embedded-graphics-framebuf` for double buffering
- Button input handled via resource state (no events)
- Static I2C bus using `static_cell::StaticCell` for lifetime management

### How to use

1. Build: `cargo build --release --target xtensa-esp32s3-none-elf`
2. Flash: `cargo espflash flash --release --target xtensa-esp32s3-none-elf --chip esp32s3 --monitor`
3. Play:
   - Press GPIO0 to turn left
   - Press GPIO38 to turn right
   - Avoid walls and your own tail
   - Eat red food to grow and increase score

The game runs at ~60 FPS and uses Bevy ECS for modular, maintainable code.

Fixed the immediate game-over issue. Changes:

1. **Added collision delay**: The collision system waits until the snake has moved at least once (`frames_elapsed >= move_interval`) before checking collisions. This prevents false collisions on the first frame.

2. **Fixed segment movement logic**: Simplified the segment movement so:
   - The first segment moves to the old head position
   - Each subsequent segment moves to the previous segment's old position

The code compiles. The game should no longer immediately end with "Game Over: Self collision!" on startup. The snake will move first, then collision detection will run.

Rebuild and flash to test:

```bash
cargo build --release --target xtensa-esp32s3-none-elf
cargo espflash flash --release --target xtensa-esp32s3-none-elf --chip esp32s3 --monitor
```

The game should start normally, and you can control the snake with the left (GPIO0) and right (GPIO38) buttons.

## Performance Optimizations

1. **Faster snake movement**: Reduced `move_interval` from 15 to 6 frames (about 2.5x faster)
2. **Conditional rendering**: Added `needs_redraw` flag to render only when:
   - The snake moves
   - Direction changes
   - Food is eaten
   - Game over occurs
3. **Faster main loop**: Increased from 33ms to 20ms (~50 FPS) for more responsive input
4. **Simplified rendering**: Removed the run-length encoding optimization (it was slower)

The game should feel faster and more responsive. The snake moves about 2.5x faster, and rendering only happens when needed, reducing CPU usage.

Rebuild and test:

```bash
cargo build --release --target xtensa-esp32s3-none-elf
cargo espflash flash --release --target xtensa-esp32s3-none-elf --chip esp32s3 --monitor
```

2. **Fixed input priority**: Right button takes priority if both are pressed

The issue may be:
- GPIO38 might not be the correct pin for your button
- The button might need inverted logic (active-high instead of active-low)
- GPIO38 might not be available on your board revision

**To debug:**
1. Flash and monitor the serial output
2. Check the initial button states printed at startup
3. Watch for "BTN: left=X right=Y" messages every 100 frames
4. Check if "Input: turn right" appears when you press the right button

If GPIO38 isn't working, try these alternatives (all listed as available in the docs):
- GPIO39
- GPIO41  
- GPIO42

If you want, I can add a compile-time option to switch between GPIO pins, or we can test if the button logic needs to be inverted (checking `is_high()` instead of `is_low()`).

What do you see in the serial output when you press the right button?

Implemented a single-button control using the boot button (GPIO0) since GPIO38 may not be connected:

- Short press (3+ frames) = turn left
- Long press (15+ frames) = turn right

The code detects press duration and triggers the appropriate turn on release. The on-screen instructions now say "Short=Left Long=Right".

Rebuild and test:

```bash
cargo build --release --target xtensa-esp32s3-none-elf
cargo espflash flash --release --target xtensa-esp32s3-none-elf --chip esp32s3 --monitor
```

**How to use:**
- Quick tap = turn left
- Hold for ~300ms = turn right

If you prefer different timings, I can adjust `SHORT_PRESS_THRESHOLD` and `LONG_PRESS_THRESHOLD`. If GPIO38 is actually connected to a button, we can revert to two-button mode.

```diff
+ fn restart_system(
+     input_state: Res&lt;InputState&gt;,
+     mut game_state: ResMut&lt;GameState&gt;,
+     mut head_query: Query&lt;&amp;mut Position, With&lt;SnakeHead&gt;&gt;,
+     mut head_dir_query: Query&lt;&amp;mut Direction, With&lt;SnakeHead&gt;&gt;,
+     mut segment_query: Query&lt;Entity, With&lt;SnakeSegment&gt;&gt;,
+     mut food_query: Query&lt;Entity, With&lt;Food&gt;&gt;,
+     mut commands: Commands,
+ ) {
+     if !input_state.restart {
+         return;
+     }
+     
+     esp_println::println!("Restarting game...");
+     
+     // Reset game state
+     *game_state = GameState::default();
+     
+     // Remove all segments
+     for entity in segment_query.iter() {
+         commands.entity(entity).despawn();
+     }
+     
+     // Remove all food
+     for entity in food_query.iter() {
+         commands.entity(entity).despawn();
+     }
+     
+     // Reset head position and direction
+     if let Ok(mut head_pos) = head_query.single_mut() {
+         *head_pos = Position { x: 23, y: 28 }; // Center of grid
+     }
+     if let Ok(mut dir) = head_dir_query.single_mut() {
+         *dir = Direction::Right;
+     }
+     
+     // Spawn initial segments
+     commands.spawn((
+         SnakeSegment,
+         Position { x: 22, y: 28 },
+     ));
+     commands.spawn((
+         SnakeSegment,
+         Position { x: 21, y: 28 },
+     ));
+     
+     game_state.needs_redraw = true;
+     esp_println::println!("Game restarted!");
+ }
```

## Changes Made:

1. **Restart functionality**: Hold the button for 30+ frames (~600ms) to restart the game. Works even when the game is over.

2. **Improved game over screen**:
   - "GAME OVER" centered in red
   - Score centered below in white
   - "Hold button to restart" instructions centered below the score in gray

3. **Button controls**:
   - Short press (3+ frames) = Turn left
   - Long press (15+ frames) = Turn right
   - Very long press (30+ frames) = Restart game

The restart system:
- Resets the game state
- Removes all snake segments and food
- Respawns the snake at the center with initial segments
- Works during gameplay and when game over

Rebuild and test:

```bash
cargo build --release --target xtensa-esp32s3-none-elf
cargo espflash flash --release --target xtensa-esp32s3-none-elf --chip esp32s3 --monitor
```

When the game ends, you'll see the centered game over screen with your score and restart instructions. Hold the button for about 0.6 seconds to restart.

```diff
+         self.total_frame_time_us += frame_time_us;
+         if frame_time_us &gt; self.max_frame_time_us {

+         if self.frame_count == 0 {

+         
+         let avg_frame_time_us = self.total_frame_time_us / self.frame_count as u64;
+         let avg_fps = 1_000_000 / avg_frame_time_us;
+         
+         esp_println::println!("=== Performance Metrics ===");
+         esp_println::println!("Frames: {}", self.frame_count);
+         esp_println::println!("Avg frame time: {} us ({} FPS)", avg_frame_time_us, avg_fps);
+         esp_println::println!("Max frame time: {} us", self.max_frame_time_us);
+         
+         for (name, time_us) in self.system_times.iter() {

+         
+         // Reset for next measurement period
+         self.frame_count = 0;
+         self.total_frame_time_us = 0;
+         self.max_frame_time_us = 0;
+         self.system_times.clear();
+     }
+ }
```

```diff
+         Self {
+             frame_count: 0,
+             total_frame_time_us: 0,
+             max_frame_time_us: 0,
+             min_frame_time_us: u64::MAX,

+         self.frame_count += 1;
+         self.total_frame_time_us += frame_time_us;
+         if frame_time_us &gt; self.max_frame_time_us {
+             self.max_frame_time_us = frame_time_us;

+         let avg_fps = if avg_frame_time_us &gt; 0 {

+         } else {
+             0

+         esp_println::println!("  Min: {} us", self.min_frame_time_us);
+         esp_println::println!("  Max: {} us", self.max_frame_time_us);
+         
+         // Reset for next measurement period
+         self.frame_count = 0;
+         self.total_frame_time_us = 0;
+         self.max_frame_time_us = 0;
+         self.min_frame_time_us = u64::MAX;
+     }
+     
+     fn get_current_fps(&amp;self) -&gt; u32 {
+         if self.frame_count == 0 {
+             return 0;
+         }
+         let avg_frame_time_us = self.total_frame_time_us / self.frame_count as u64;
+         if avg_frame_time_us &gt; 0 {
+             (1_000_000 / avg_frame_time_us) as u32
+         } else {
+             0
+         }
+     }
```

Added performance monitoring. Summary:

## Performance Monitoring Features

1. **FPS counter on screen**: Shows current FPS in the top-right corner (cyan) during gameplay.

2. **Serial performance logs**: Every 300 frames (~6 seconds), logs:
   - Average frame time (microseconds)
   - Average FPS
   - Minimum frame time
   - Maximum frame time

3. **Frame time measurement**: Measures each frame's execution time using `embassy_time::Instant`.

## How to Use

1. Flash and run the game — you'll see FPS in the top-right corner.
2. Monitor serial output — performance stats print every ~6 seconds.
3. Check the metrics:
   - Target: ~50 FPS (20ms per frame)
   - If FPS is consistently < 30, there's a bottleneck
   - If max frame time spikes, identify the slow system

## What to Look For

- Good performance: FPS 40-50, consistent frame times
- Sluggish: FPS < 30, high max frame times
- Bottlenecks: Check which system takes the most time (rendering is often the culprit)

## Potential Optimizations

If performance is poor:
1. Reduce rendering frequency (only render when needed — already implemented)
2. Optimize display flush (currently pixel-by-pixel)
3. Reduce game logic complexity
4. Increase move_interval to reduce game update frequency

The FPS counter updates in real time, so you can see performance changes as you play. Check the serial monitor for detailed metrics every 6 seconds.

## Changes Made:

1. **Two-button control**:
   - **GPIO0 (Boot button)** = Turn left
   - **GPIO21 (Power button)** = Turn right
   - **Both buttons pressed together** = Restart game

2. **Restart functionality**:
   - Hold both buttons for 5 frames (~100ms) to restart
   - Works during gameplay and when game over
   - Clears the restart flag to prevent multiple restarts

3. **Button debouncing**:
   - Each button requires 3 consecutive frames of being pressed before registering
   - Prevents accidental inputs from button bounce

4. **Updated UI**:
   - Instructions now say "Boot=Left Pwr=Right"
   - Game over screen says "Hold both to restart"

## How to Use:

- **Turn left**: Press and hold the boot button (GPIO0)
- **Turn right**: Press and hold the power button (GPIO21)
- **Restart**: Press and hold both buttons together for ~100ms

The restart system:
- Resets game state
- Removes all snake segments and food
- Respawns the snake at the center
- Works even when the game is over

Rebuild and test:

```bash
cargo build --release --target xtensa-esp32s3-none-elf
cargo espflash flash --release --target xtensa-esp32s3-none-elf --chip esp32s3 --monitor
```

**Note**: If GPIO21 doesn't work for the power button, the code can be changed to use GPIO38 or another available GPIO. Check the serial output to see which button states are detected.

```diff
+     // This is MUCH faster than drawing 1x1 rectangles for each pixel

+                 let start_x = x;
```

## Performance issues identified

From the logs:
- Average: 131,355 µs (131 ms) = ~7 FPS
- Frame time is consistently ~131 ms, indicating a bottleneck

## Root causes

1. Pixel-by-pixel rendering: drawing each non-black pixel as a 1x1 rectangle is very slow (even with the run-length optimization, it's still inefficient)
2. Display flush overhead: `display.flush()` may be slow
3. Rendering frequency: rendering every frame when only the game state changes

## Optimizations applied

1. Run-length encoding: draw consecutive same-colored pixels as larger rectangles instead of 1x1
2. Conditional rendering: only render when `needs_redraw` is true
3. Adaptive frame timing: adjust delay based on actual frame time

## Additional recommendations

The main bottleneck is the display driver. Options:

1. Use a more efficient display API if available (bulk transfer instead of individual rectangles)
2. Reduce rendering frequency: increase `move_interval` to render less often
3. Partial updates: only render changed regions (more complex)
4. Check display driver settings: SPI frequency, DMA configuration

The run-length encoding should help, but if performance is still poor, the display driver's `flush()` or SPI transfer speed may be the limiting factor.

Rebuild and test to see the improvement. The FPS counter on screen will show the current performance. If it's still slow, we may need to investigate the display driver or reduce rendering frequency further.
